transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. It's nice to meet you; could you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Hi, Dr. Smith. Um, I came in because my sleep is just all broken up now. I get off an overnight shift at work and I just... I still lie there wide awake. Then when I finally do drift off, I wake up scared, and I just feel like I never rested at all.
When you wake up scared, do you find that you are having vivid, distressing dreams about a specific past event that felt dangerous or life-threatening?

No, it's not like that. I don't really remember dreaming about anything specific or... or any bad events from the past. I just wake up and my heart is pounding, and I just feel this heavy sense of dread, but it's not attached to a memory or anything.
Outside of when you are trying to sleep, do you find that you spend a lot of your day feeling uncontrollably worried or anxious about various things in your life?

No, I don't think so. I mean, I'm not really worrying about things like paying bills or... or my job or anything like that. It's more just this heavy, dark feeling all the time. But it's not like I'm sitting around panicking about normal everyday stuff.
Do you find that you have lost interest in or pleasure from the activities that you usually enjoy?

Um, no, I don't think so. I still like doing the things I usually do. Like, I still watch my shows when I get home from my shift, and I still like seeing my friends. I haven't really lost interest in any of that... I just have that heavy feeling while I'm doing it, I guess. But I still enjoy my normal stuff.
Has anyone ever mentioned that you snore loudly or stop breathing while you are asleep?
No, nobody's ever said anything like that to me. I don't think I snore, or at least, no one has ever complained about it. And I haven't heard anything about stopping breathing, either.
During the day, when you are not at work, do you find yourself feeling so sleepy that you struggle to stay awake or find yourself nodding off?
No, not really. I mean, I might feel a little tired sometimes, but I'm not nodding off or struggling to keep my eyes open during the day. I stay awake just fine when I'm off work.
Does your difficulty falling asleep and your feeling of dread occur only on the days following your overnight shifts, or do you experience these same symptoms even on your days off?

It's both. It happens on my days off, too. That's actually why I came in, because my sleep is just all broken up now. Like, I'll get off an overnight shift and just lie there wide awake in bed when I should be exhausted. But even on my days off, it's the exact same thing. And then when I finally do drift off, I wake up scared... and I just feel like I never rested at all.
When you are on your days off, do you find yourself wanting to go to sleep much later or much earlier than you actually do?
No, I don't really want to go to sleep earlier or later. I just want to go to sleep at a normal time, like I used to. But I just can't.
When you wake up after those periods of broken sleep, do you typically find yourself waking up much earlier than you intended to, and are you unable to fall back asleep?

No, I don't really wake up earlier than I want to. I just wake up a lot during the night. I eventually fall back asleep, but it's just broken up all night long. I never wake up and just stay awake for the rest of the morning.
When you are lying in bed trying to fall asleep at the start of your night, how long does it typically take you to actually drift off?
I don't know exactly. I haven't really timed it or anything. It just feels like I'm lying there for a long time, tossing and turning, before I finally fall asleep.
When you are lying in bed trying to fall asleep, is your mind racing with thoughts, or are you mostly just frustrated by the physical sensation of being unable to drift off?

I don't really think my mind is racing. I haven't noticed a bunch of thoughts going on or anything like that. And... I don't know if I'm frustrated, really. I just mostly lie there in the quiet, waiting to finally fall asleep.
Over the past three months, how many nights per week, on average, do you experience this difficulty falling or staying asleep?

It's pretty much every day. That's actually why I came in, because my sleep is just all broken up now. I'll get off an overnight shift and still just lie there wide awake. Then when I finally do drift off, I wake up scared and feel like I never rested at all.
Does this ongoing issue with your sleep cause you significant distress or interfere with your ability to function during the day, such as at work or in your social life?

Yes, it's definitely interfering with everything. I can't keep up with my care visits safely anymore. Just the other day, my supervisor actually had to stop me during a care-plan visit because I was just... too overwhelmed. I felt totally stuck and couldn't even finish it. And outside of work, I've completely pulled away from everything else. I used to go to church, take Zumba classes, and do some mentoring, but I've stopped all of it. I can barely manage just getting through work and getting back home.

You mentioned earlier that you still enjoyed your normal activities, but just now you said you've stopped your church, Zumba, and mentoring; would you say you stopped these activities because you no longer find them enjoyable, or for some other reason?
I... I don't really know if I still enjoy them or not. I just don't have the energy for them anymore. I used to like them, but now... I just can't bring myself to go. It's just too much.
Have you noticed any significant changes in your appetite or your weight lately, without trying to change your diet?
No, not really. My appetite is pretty much the same as it's always been, and my weight hasn't changed either.
Have you noticed that your movements or your speech have become noticeably slower, or conversely, that you feel physically restless and unable to sit still?

Yeah, I have. Everything I do has gotten really slow. Even just... putting on my scrubs in the morning takes forever. And answering a question, like now, it just feels like it takes me longer to get the words out. People at work have actually brought it up. They keep telling me I just stand there staring, like I can't even make myself move.
Do you find yourself frequently feeling worthless or like you are a burden to others, or perhaps feeling guilty about things that you haven't done or that are out of your control?

Yeah, all the time. I just... I keep going over every little thing I ever did wrong with my patients or my family. It makes me feel like I'm just a worthless aide. And honestly, it feels like God is mad at me for not protecting people better. I just can't stop thinking about it.
